prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational. Asset: production sprite atlas for Cosmic: A Sea Beneath the Moon. Input image1 is a STYLE reference only: retain the medallion form, palette, grain and physical depiction approach, but create the NEW requested subjects below. Exactly 4 columns by 4 rows, 16 circles total. Regular equal square cells, Use a SQUARE canvas, exactly 4 columns by 4 rows, equal square cells, no outer margin. Aim2048px wide. Every circle diameter84%of its cell, centred, with generous fully transparent gutters; leave allcells complete and separated. No extra cells or objects. Original astronomical chromolithograph with dry-gouache and chalk masses: deep indigo circular fields, feathered warm-ivory light, amber heat, copper/charcoal minerals and restrained teal water. Simplify to broad meaningful structures visible at72px. Fine grain stays in subjects; generous quiet dark space. One thin ivory circular outline. No glossy UI buttons, photographic lens flare, ornamental decoration, humans, machines, text, labels, numerals, formulas or grid lines. Inside each circle the field is opaque; outside circles true alpha transparency. No shadows, rays or fragments beyond circles. Atom/particle diagrams are schematic: tiny compact ivory dots and diffuse electron-probability clouds, never planetary electron orbits; individual nuclei do NOT glow like stars. Exact invisible chemistry is communicated by game names/readings, never by invented diagnostic coloration. All terrestrial worlds have bare mineral terrain; no plants, life or modern continents. Early Moon is pale gray-ivory without familiar dark maria. All Earth cutaways are views of one continuing world.
Strict row-major subjects (left to right, then top to bottom):
1. Oxygen on a grain: One enlarged rough dust grain with one soft ivory adsorbate cloud touching its upper edge. Avoid: Schematic surface atom, not an ice coating or visible chemical paint.
2. Hydroxyl on a grain: The same grain with one two-lobed bonded adsorbate attached to the same upper edge. Avoid: Schematic bonded pair; no bulk ice mantle yet and no letters or formula.
3. Ice-mantled dust: The same rough dark grain covered by a continuous thin translucent ivory ice mantle. Avoid: Mantle on a grain, not free-floating snowflakes or a liquid droplet.
4. Hydrogen molecules formed on dust: A two-lobed hydrogen molecule just above an enlarged dark grain surface, departing on a short sparse cue. Avoid: Same H2 molecule as earlier; substrate distinguishes formation route only.
5. A cold molecular cloud: A deep dark cloud with broad feathered pale rim and dense branching interior dust structures. Avoid: Cold shielded gas reservoir; no internal stars and no literal visible molecules at cloud scale.
6. A contracting cloud filament: A long bent dusty filament with two dense knots and short converging flow strokes. Avoid: Elongated contraction, not a rotating disk or already lit protostar.
7. The cloud’s slow rotation: A broad diffuse gas patch with two sparse curved directional strokes about a loose centre. Avoid: Slow rotation of an extended cloud; no rigid wheel or complete disk.
8. A magnetic field in the gas: Sparse curved field-line convention threads a diffuse gas patch and bends toward two opposite poles. Avoid: No rigid axle, bar magnet, iron filings or complete orbital track.
9. A rotating collapsing core: A flattened dusty gas core with two broad infalling curved arms and a small dense unlit centre. Avoid: Collapsing core with thick arms; no established central Sun yet.
10. The Sun’s protostar: A warm compact luminous centre cocooned in a thick flattened dusty envelope, short infalling arms. Avoid: Use dusty solar family unlike the dust-free first protostar.
11. The contracting young Sun: A warm ivory-amber Sun emerges from a thin residual equatorial veil, with uneven soft rays. Avoid: Same solar source thereafter; no assertion that main-sequence fusion has begun.
12. A planet-forming solar disk: A broad tilted ellipse of gas and dusty material around the small established young Sun, open dark surroundings. Avoid: Solar disk contains a luminous star; lunar disk surrounds cracked molten Earth.
13. A protostellar outflow: The dusty protostar and thin equatorial disk emit two opposing broad tapered plumes perpendicular to the disk. Avoid: Bipolar material outflow, not laser beams or a supernova.
14. Sunlight: The established small warm young Sun at one edge sends long uneven ivory rays across the field. Avoid: Keep solar identity and warmth; Moon is a separate reflected-light body.
15. A disk with a hot inner region: The same tilted solar disk with a strongly luminous warm inner zone and a dim cool outer zone. Avoid: Heat gradient in one disk; no hard snow-line boundary or planets.
16. A cavity through the natal cloud: Two broad dark openings cut through a pale natal cloud above and below a small surviving equatorial disk. Avoid: Emptied lobes, not solid cones or the disappearance of the disk.
